newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks end slightly up on volume trade.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks end slightly up on volume trade.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed a shade up on volume trading of inexpensive shares, as investors assessed the year's potential before committing big, brokers said.
The all share index closed 0.4 points higher at 607.1 in active trading which saw gains outnumbering losses 29 to 19.
"The same people who sold at the end of last year are buying now, hoping prices will go up in the new year," said Gordon Nadesan, assistant sales manager at CT Smith Stockbrokers.
Turnover was 42.6 million rupees, supported by 112,000 Blue Diamonds at 10.75 rupees, about 600,000 Grain Elevators at 14.75, 608,400 Dockyard at 14.50, 270,000 Sampath Bank at 46.
"Investors are still trying to figure out the market before making bigger commitments," said Namal Kamalgoda, fund manager equities at CTC Eagle. "So far the trend is quite positive."

The main declining stocks were Commercial Bank and Hatton National Bank, which fell five rupees and eight rupees each to 129 and 265 rupees respectively, due mainly to speculation involving a possible merger of the two companies, brokers said.
Commercial Bank said on Thursday, that Hatton National and Development Finance Corporation had bidded for a 40 percent stake of its equity.
